title: Instrumentation handoff playbook for inference teams
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for handing off observability (metrics, traces, dashboards) from feature owners (inference feature teams) to the observability team and long-term owners. It is intentionally lightweight — follow these steps when a change touches the serving runtime, routing, batching, caching, or any component that materially affects latency, throughput, or cost.

Scope:
- Applies to feature work that will be deployed to host/dedicated/private inference stacks.
- Focus is on signal design and ownership: what to instrument, how to name it, expected baselines, and how dashboards/SLOs map to the metric set.
- Not a replacement for SDK-level instrumentation guides (see linked Confluence doc), but a checklist for handoff and short-term verification.

Quick checklist (what to deliver with a PR):
- [ ] Metric names & units documented (see Metric Definitions below)
- [ ] Trace/span design doc attached (one paragraph + example span JSON)
- [ ] Dashboard mock screenshot (Grafana/Looker) + list of panels and queries
- [ ] Suggested SLI/SLO mapping and burn rate expectations
- [ ] Cost-awareness notes (expected token/cycle delta)
- [ ] Alert proposals (target thresholds, on-call play)
- [ ] Testing plan: synthetic load + smoke traces collected

Metric definitions (canonical examples, copy/adapt for feature):
- inference.request.count
  - owner: feature-team (primary), eng-observability (secondary)
  - type: counter
  - unit: requests
  - description: total number of top-level inference requests received by the service (HTTP POSTs).
  - aggregation: sum per minute; cardinality: low (per-route, per-region)

- inference.request.latency_ms
  - owner: feature-team
  - type: histogram (buckets) + summary (p50/p95/p99)
  - unit: milliseconds
  - description: end-to-end processing latency from request receive to first byte of response streamed.
  - note: prefer histogram for dashboarding; record per-request with route and model_version tags.

- inference.kv_cache.hit_rate
  - owner: feature-team
  - type: gauge (derived)
  - unit: ratio (0-1)
  - description: rolling hit-rate of prefix/KV cache for this model shard.
  - calculation: hits / (hits + misses) over 5m window; tag by model_variant and shard_id.

- inference.ejected_requests.count
  - owner: eng-sre/feature-team (shared)
  - type: counter
  - unit: requests
  - description: number of requests explicitly ejected or rejected due to overload, auth, or fallback policies.
  - labels: reason, tenant_id, route_id.

- inference.model.quantized_count
  - owner: infra/release-engineering
  - type: gauge
  - unit: instances
  - description: number of serving instances running a quantized variant. Useful for cost attribution.

Metric naming conventions (short reminders):
- Use prefix inference.<component>.<signal> (e.g., inference.kv_cache.latency_ms)
- Avoid freeform high-cardinality labels (no raw user ids in metrics; use tenant_id hashed or coarse tenant tiers)
- Each metric must have a documented owner and intended aggregation.

Tracing: span design and sampling guidance
- Top-level span: inference.request (one per incoming HTTP request). Attributes: request_id, route, model_version, tenant_tier, seq_len_hint, routed_region.
- Important child spans:
  - routing.lookup (time to route request to shard/variant)
  - model.load_weights (if lazy-load path used; high latency expected occasionally)
  - kv_cache.lookup (include cache_hit boolean attribute)
  - batcher.wait (time spent queued in batching layer)
  - runtime.decode_and_generate (actual token generation loop)
- Span attributes (keep small, low-cardinality): route, model_version, shard_id, cache_hit, batch_size, gpu_type, quantized_variant.
- Sampling policy:
  - Always sample 1 in 200 requests across the fleet (default).
  - For requests with latency > p95 or errors, force-sample 100% for 10 minutes (burst capture) to assist RCA.
  - For tenants with active incident, raise sampling to 1 in 20 for the tenant_id (tagged).

Dashboards: composition and pragmatic notes
- Minimum panels for any new feature:
  1) Traffic & errors: inference.request.count / inference.ejected_requests.count (by route)
  2) Latency heatmap: p50/p95/p99 and bucketed histogram for latency_ms
  3) Cost proxy: tokens_per_request aggregated * model_cost_per_token (rough estimate)
  4) Cache view: kv_cache.hit_rate and raw misses (to validate caching assumptions)
  5) Trace sample stream: recent sampled traces for the route
- Panel design: prefer 1-3 queries per panel; annotate expected baselines and normal ranges in the panel description.
- Per-tenant view: only expose tenant-level breakdowns when necessary; use tenant tiers (free/standard/enterprise) rather than raw tenant ids.
- Dashboard lifecycle: add a "sunset" tag and ownership in panel meta. If feature is experimental, mark dashboard status=ephemeral and schedule review in 30d.

Rollout verification (smoke tests to run post-deploy):
- Synthetic load that targets new route at production-like QPS for 10 minutes. Verify p95 latency within expected bound and no increase in ejected_requests > 0.5% of traffic.
- Generate traces for both cache-hit and cache-miss paths to confirm span shapes and attributes.
- Validate metric ingestion (count cardinality and absence of high-cardinality labels).
- Confirm dashboard panels render without expensive queries (run time < 5s for full timeframe).

Alerting guidance
- Prefer SLO-aligned alerts (burn-rate/errbudget) for customer-impacting signals.
- Operational alerts: e.g., sudden drop in kv_cache.hit_rate (delta > 15% vs 1h baseline) or sharp increase in batcher.wait above threshold. Include runbook link.
- Avoid noisy alerts: require 5m sustained condition and cross-check with traffic volume before paging.

Ownership and handoff steps (who does what)
- Feature owner responsibilities (pre-handoff): draft metric doc, span sketch, dashboard mock, synthetic test plan.
- Observability owner responsibilities (post-handoff): review metrics for cardinality/aggregation, align on SLOs, wire dashboards into central folder and assign long-term owner, suggest alert thresholds.
- Final step: create a tiny "onboard ticket" for eng-observability (template attached in Confluence link) and assign acceptance criteria: metrics accepted, traces validated, dashboards in PROD folder.

Runbook / quick triage pointers (for pagers):
- If p95 latency spikes: check recent deploys for model_version tag; inspect batcher.wait and runtime.decode_and_generate spans; look for model.load_weights spikes.
- If requests are ejected: check quota/policy changes and ejected_requests.reason, correlate with upstream auth or rate-limit rules.
- If cost unexpectedly increases: compare tokens_per_request and quantized_variant counts; verify model routing did not mistakenly shift to larger model.

Examples / small fragment to copy into a PR (span example):
- Top-level span: {"name": "inference.request", "attrs": {"request_id": "req-12345", "route": "chat-completion-v2", "model_version": "rwd-v1.3", "tenant_tier": "standard"}}
- Child span example: {"name": "kv_cache.lookup", "attrs": {"cache_hit": "true", "shard_id": "s-12"}}
(Keep JSON examples small; full SDK annotation guidelines in Confluence doc.)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need a separate cost SLI that tracks model-weight-hours for ephemeral scale-ups? (cc: infra-costs)
- How aggressive should tenant-specific sampling be for high-volume customers? (privacy and perf tradeoffs)
- Need a quick utility to validate metric cardinality on PRs (follow-up task INF-812).

Notes to self / editorial: this playbook should be used for both Hosted and Dedicated rollouts. For Private/on-prem customers, ensure the KMS/PII guidance is attached when traces may include tenant identifiers.

References and linked templates:
- Confluence: OBS-INSTRUMENTATION-ONBOARDING (detailed SDK examples and PR checklist)
- GitHub template: infra/pull_request_templates/obs-instrumentation.md
- JIRA templates: INF-PR-INSTRUMENTATION (for handoff tickets)

If you're reviewing: please add comments inline on ambiguous metric names or anything that might explode cardinality. We will iterate fast — the goal is observable, debuggable launches, not perfect instrumentation on day 0.

-- Asha
